question.text: When <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> moles of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>He</mi></math> gas expand isothermally and reversibly at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>300</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn></math> litre to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn></math> litre, the magnitude of the maximum work obtained is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>. [nearest integer ] (Given : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3010</mn></math>)

solution.text:
Work done in isothermal reversible process is calculated by the equation

W=-2.303nRTlogV2V1n=Number of molesT=Temperature=300KV2=Final volume=20 litresV1=Initial volume=10 litres   

W=-2.303×5×8.3×300log2010

=-8630.38 J
